corrections.to: basis vectors with overlap eigenvalue below 1e-7 removed (near linear dependence; Appendix A.1)
corrections.reported_as: For the largest basis sets cc-pVTZ, cc-pVQZ, and cc-pV5Z at geometries R < 1.6 aB and cc-pVDZ at R < 1.4 aB, the Gaussian basis is nearly linearly dependent. We remove linearly dependent vectors with an overlap threshold of 10^-7. Although a smaller threshold could be used in the Hartree-Fock calculation, changing the energy by ~10^-6 EHa per atom, we find the resulting CCSD calculations with smaller thresholds to be numerically unstable.
corrections.location: PRX 7, 031059, Appendix A.1 (coupled cluster), p. 031059-13; same text arXiv v2 line 790-800 of sources/1705.01608.txt; main text Sec. V A: 'To deal with basis-set linear dependence, which becomes relevant at the shortest bond lengths and largest basis sets, we apply a threshold to eigenvalues of the overlap matrix.'
corrections.reason: R = 1 bohr, cc-pV5Z: inside the paper's stated linear-dependence window, so the energy is for the cc-pVxZ space with near-null vectors removed (paper: about 1e-6 Eh per atom effect on HF). The row should say so; value unchanged. The paper states the threshold in the CC subsection, whose RHF references the dataset RHF files most plausibly are.
